Subject: High-context streaming — pricing question

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One follow-up: our product streams long documents in ~10–20k token chunks, split across many short-lived sessions. Our engineering team measured what they call 'rounding waste' — because each streaming segment is billed per-request with a 25-token quantum, we're seeing ~12% extra billed tokens on average versus raw token counts.

Can Redwood accommodate a different billing model for this workload? Ideally something that reduces rounding waste (we'd accept a temporary credit or a contract-level smoothing/aggregation that applies to the monthly invoice). We're targeting 150k–300k effective tokens/day initially.

If you need any runtime traces or a sample of call-level token counts we can share those.

Best,
Susan Park
Lead Product, Acme Conversational

Hi Susan,

Really appreciate the detail and the sample log. Short answer: yes — we can offer a smoothing/credit mechanism for customers with high-volume, long-sequence streaming patterns.

I'm attaching a provisional spreadsheet with a couple of approaches:
- rolling-window smoothing (compute per-call rounding waste over a 10-minute window and apply a monthly credit equal to X% of that waste),
- per-session aggregation (server-side merge of small segments into a single billable unit when segments are contiguous and within the same logical session).

Before I lock anything in with legal/finance I want to check internal constraints. Looping in Marissa and Karthik to propose a concrete number and confirm accounting treatment.

High level ask to you: can you confirm an expected average segment size and the relative frequency of contiguous segments (e.g., 60% of segments are part of a session that lasts < 2 minutes; 25% are > 5 minutes, etc.)? That helps pick the right window.

Thanks — will follow up with a concrete proposal by EOD Fri.

Looping you in on Acme's ask (below). They have significant rounding waste from small streaming segments and would prefer either a smoothing credit applied monthly or a contract-level aggregation rule.

Key constraints I think we should consider:
- We can't change the base per-token price in the portal for a single customer without a negotiated contract.
- Finance prefers credits on invoices over altering metering primitives for the sandbox.

Example data point from Susan: average segment billed quantum is 25 tokens; measured average segment actual tokens = 18. Effective rounding waste ~= 7 tokens per segment -> ~38% overhead for those calls. With 200k effective tokens/day that can move the bill by a material %.

Questions for pricing/billing:
1) If we compute 'monthly smoothing credit = S% * (sum of per-call rounding waste)', can we apply that as a single invoice credit line? Any ledger/GL limits?
2) What guardrails should we set (max credit cap, minimum commitment)?
3) Any objections to doing a 3-month pilot with an elevated smoothing rate?

Would like concrete language I can send to Susan so legal can start a playbook thread.

- Naomi

Thanks Naomi — good summary. My recommended operational proposal:

Proposal A (smoothing credit pilot) — recommended for Sales pilot:
- Metering remains unchanged. We compute per-call rounding waste = billed_quanta * quantum_size - actual_tokens, summed monthly.
- Pilot smoothing credit = 50% of the monthly rounding waste (expressed in token-equivalent dollars), applied as a single credit line on the invoice.
- Pilot duration = 3 months.
- Quantum size used here = 25 tokens (matches current runtime).
- Cap: credit cannot exceed 30% of the invoice subtotal.

Example (simple):
- Month raw billed tokens (pre-credit) = 9,000,000 tokens
- Computed rounding waste = 450,000 tokens (5% of billed due to quantum inefficiency)
- Pilot credit = 50% * 450,000 = 225,000 token-equivalent -> credit applied as $ = 225,000 * per-token-rate
- Post-credit bill = billed_amount - credit (credit visible as negative line on invoice).

Rationale: keeps metering stable, gives the customer immediate economics relief, and is simple from an implementation perspective (off-invoice credit).

Operational notes:
- Need clarity from finance if 30% cap can be reduced/raised for specific large deals.
- For longer-term we should offer a contract amendment that instead changes the quantum for that customer's dedicated endpoints (reduces waste at the source), but that requires runtime/config changes and product approval.

If this looks good I can author the pricing clause language for SOW.

- Karthik
Lead, Pricing & Packaging

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FW: High-context streaming — fractional rounding ask

Couple of accounting/billing constraints to keep in mind before we promise the customer anything material:

1) Invoice representation: we cannot modify historical usage lines. Credits must be applied as separate line items ("Smoothing credit - ACME") and posted to the invoice as a contra-revenue line. That's acceptable; legal/finance will need the GL code.
2) Refunds vs credits: we prefer invoice credits (not refunds) because refunds trigger extra approval flows and payment processor work.
3) Approval thresholds: credits over $50k require VP-Finance signoff. For pilots we can do up to $50k without escalations.

Operational guardrails suggestion (practical):
- Pilot = 3 months, smoothing credit = 50% of computed rounding waste, cap = 30% of invoice, explicit minimum committed spend = $75k/month,
- If usage grows beyond 500k effective tokens/day we transition to a contract amendment that adjusts quantum or moves them to a dedicated endpoint with custom metering.

I'll coordinate with billing ops to make sure we can produce the computed rounding report each month and apply the credit programmatically.

- Vivek
Head of Finance Operations

Subject: Proposed smoothing pilot — Acme / Redwood

Hi Susan,

Thanks for the sample logs and for your patience while we coordinated internally. Below is the proposed pilot we can put in the SOW (attached):

Summary (pilot)
- Duration: 3 months starting on the first invoice month after signature.
- Metering: no change to runtime metering (we keep the 25-token quantum).
- Computation: each month Redwood will compute the customer's per-call rounding waste (billed_quanta*25 - actual_tokens) across eligible streaming segments and sum to a monthly token-equivalent waste.
- Credit: Redwood will grant a smoothing credit equal to 50% of the computed token-equivalent waste (converted to dollars at the negotiated per-token rate).
- Cap & minimums: credit capped at 30% of invoice subtotal; minimum committed spend during pilot = $75k/month.
- Escalation/transition: if average effective tokens/day > 500k we will engage product to discuss a runtime quantum change or move to a dedicated endpoint with custom metering.

Examples: (illustrative only)
- If billed pre-credit = $45,000 and computed rounding waste = 225,000 tokens and per-token rate = $0.0001, pilot credit = 225,000 * 0.0001 * 50% = $11.25 -> credit applied as invoice line item.

Attached: SOW_Acme_v1.pdf (draft clause + acceptance block), provisional-pricing-spreadsheet.xlsx (worked examples).

If this looks good to you I'll route to Legal for a short amendment and instruct Finance to prepare the monthly rounding report. Please confirm and if you prefer a different pilot credit percentage (we can be flexible but will need adjust caps).

Best,
Naomi
